```{r}
} else {
```

Our raw dataset has 713014 SNPs and 192 individuals

# Add metadata

```{r}
# Read in Pierron Malagasy metadata
pop_table <- read.table(path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_Borneo.poptable"), sep = "\t", fill = TRUE)
colnames(pop_table) <- c("IID", "V2", "FID", "Population", "V5", "V6", "V7")

# Add "RR" to pop_table$IID
pop_table$IID <- paste0(pop_table$IID, "RR")

# Find Malagasy entries
pop_table_sub <- subset(pop_table, pop_table$IID %in% madagascar$id & pop_table$V5 == "Madagascar")

# match up the ID's with pop table metadata
matching_m <- match(madagascar$id, pop_table_sub$IID)

madagascar$population <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), pop_table_sub$Population[matching_m], madagascar$population)
```

# Check and remove the random "I" loci

```{r}
remove <- which(show_loci(madagascar)$allele_ref == "I")
madagascar <- madagascar %>% select_loci(-all_of(c(remove)))
count_loci(madagascar)
```

# Update build

Add a section here with the biomart function/find a better way to do this?

First, new bim
```{r}
new_bim_no_NA <- read.table(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/intermediate/Madagascar_full_HG38.bim"), header = FALSE)
colnames(new_bim_no_NA) <- c("chromosome", "snp_id", "genetic_dist", "physical_pos", "allele1", "allele2")

nrow(new_bim_no_NA)
new_bim_no_NA <- as_tibble(new_bim_no_NA)

# subset to only autosomes
new_bim_no_NA <- new_bim_no_NA %>% filter(chromosome %in% c(1:22))

# order by chromosome
new_bim_no_NA$chromosome <- as.integer(new_bim_no_NA$chromosome)
new_bim_no_NA <- new_bim_no_NA %>% arrange(chromosome, physical_pos)
```


```{r}
# select only the loci with updated positions
madagascar <- madagascar %>% select_loci_if(loci_names(genotypes) %in% new_bim_no_NA$snp_id)

# find matching indices
match_indices <- match(show_loci(madagascar)$name, new_bim_no_NA$snp_id)
matching_rows <- !is.na(match_indices)

# update position in gt
show_loci(madagascar)$position[matching_rows] <- new_bim_no_NA$physical_pos[match_indices[matching_rows]]

# update chromosome in gt
show_loci(madagascar)$chromosome <- as.character(show_loci(madagascar)$chromosome)
show_loci(madagascar)$chromosome[matching_rows] <- new_bim_no_NA$chromosome[match_indices[matching_rows]]

# update chr_int in gt
show_loci(madagascar)$chr_int <- as.integer(show_loci(madagascar)$chromosome)
count_loci(madagascar)

# update genetic distance in gt
show_loci(madagascar)$genetic_dist[matching_rows] <- new_bim_no_NA$genetic_dist[match_indices[matching_rows]]

# remove entries with genetic distance == 0
no_dist <- which(show_loci(madagascar)$genetic_dist == 0)
madagascar <- madagascar %>% select_loci(-no_dist)

testthat::expect_false(is_loci_table_ordered(madagascar, error_on_false = FALSE, ignore_genetic_dist = TRUE))
```


# Create loci report

```{r}
madagascar <- madagascar %>% group_by(population)
loci_report_m <- qc_report_loci(madagascar)
madagascar <- madagascar %>% ungroup()

summary(loci_report_m)
autoplot(loci_report_m, type = "overview")
```

We do not want to be too stringent on filter out variants deviating from HWE, because HWE can indicate processes that we are intending to investigate (assortative mating, stratified population structures etc see Turner et al. 2011).

The grouped loci report checks hwe within sub-populations:

```{r}
to_keep <- which(loci_report_m$hwe_p > 0.01)

madagascar <- madagascar %>% select_loci(all_of(to_keep))

madagascar <- madagascar %>% ungroup()
count_loci(madagascar)
```

The following autoplots help to examine other QC measures in greater detail.

```{r}
autoplot(loci_report_m, type = "missing")
```

The automatic threshold for missingness (0.01) fits the data well, so we will stick to this threshold.

```{r}
madagascar <- madagascar %>% select_loci_if(loci_missingness(genotypes) < 0.01)
count_loci(madagascar)
```

```{r}
autoplot(loci_report_m, type = "maf")
```

The MAF distribution of this dataset has a skew? is it because of the chip used? <https://academic.oup.com/gbe/article/5/5/1021/611342>

```{r}
madagascar <- madagascar %>% select_loci_if(loci_maf(genotypes) > 0.025)
count_loci(madagascar)
```

Remove all non-autosomal SNPs.

```{r}
madagascar <- madagascar %>% select_loci_if(show_loci(genotypes)$chromosome %in% c(1:22))
count_loci(madagascar)
```

# Create individual report

```{r}
madagascar <- madagascar %>% group_by(population)
individual_report_m <- qc_report_indiv(madagascar, kings_threshold = 0.177)
madagascar <- madagascar %>% ungroup()
summary(individual_report_m)
autoplot(individual_report_m)
```

The autoplot indicates that no individuals have greater than 5% of their genotypes missing, so we do not need to filter for missingness by individual in this case.

For now, we also do not want to remove individuals with low heterozygosity, as we may want to analyse ROH across individuals in the dataset.

```{r}
autoplot(individual_report_m, type = "relatedness", kings_threshold = 0.177)
```

```{r}
madagascar <- madagascar %>% filter(id %in% individual_report_m$id & individual_report_m$to_keep == TRUE)
```

As the datasets will contain more closely related inviduals, we don't want to be too strict in removing. For now, we can remove first degree relatives.

The challenge is how to remove as few individuals as possible while still removing all relationships above this kinship threshold.

See <https://www.kingrelatedness.com/manual.shtml#>:\~:text=Close%20relatives%20can%20be%20inferred,%2Ddegree%2C%20and%203rd%2Ddegree for kinship thresholds.

```{r}
nrow(madagascar)
count_loci(madagascar)
```

Now we have a cleaned dataset, we can save this gt for future use.

```{r}
if (file.exists(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_full_cleaned.gt"))) {
  file.remove(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_full_cleaned.gt"))
}

gt_save(madagascar, file = resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_full_cleaned.gt"))
```

Next we can read in and clean other Malagasy data ready to merge with.

Very few flips but there were only 127 in previous version of flips function so don't believe this is cause for concern - weird that there are no ambiguous though??

```{r}
# Double check ambiguous

m_loci <- show_loci(madagascar)

ambiguous <- subset(
  m_loci,
  m_loci$allele_ref == "A" & m_loci$allele_alt == "T" |
    m_loci$allele_ref == "T" & m_loci$allele_alt == "A" |
    m_loci$allele_ref == "G" & m_loci$allele_alt == "C" |
    m_loci$allele_ref == "C" & m_loci$allele_alt == "G"
)
nrow(ambiguous) # looks like all ambiguous have been filtered out
```

# Check whether they are monomorphic cases

```{r}

  loci_maf()
any(maf_loci_freq > 0)
```

The Borneo dataset has a strange number of completely monomorphic SNPs. Unsure why? These can then be removed in maf filtering.

# 1000 G

Cutting down to populations of interest

```{r}
if (file.exists(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/1000_Genomes_b37_clean.gt"))) {
  g1000 <- gt_load(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/1000_Genomes_b37_clean.gt"))
} else {
  g1000 <- gen_tibble(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/1000_Genomes_b37_clean.bed"), quiet = TRUE)
}

# append population info
pop_table <- read.table(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_Borneo.poptable"), sep = "\t", fill = TRUE)
colnames(pop_table) <- c("IID", "V2", "FID", "Population", "V5", "V6", "V7")

pop_table_sub <- subset(pop_table, pop_table$IID %in% g1000$id)

matching_m <- match(g1000$id, pop_table_sub$IID)
g1000$population <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), pop_table_sub$V2[matching_m], g1000$population)

pop <- c("KHV", "BEB", "YRI", "PJL", "GWD", "MSL", "ESN", "LWK", "CHS")
#- Kinh in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
#- Bengali in Bangladesh
#- Han Chinese South
#- Luhya in Webuye, Kenya
#- Yoruba in Ibadan, Nigeria
#- Punjabi in Lahore, Pakistan
#- Gambian in Western Division, The Gambia - Mandinka
#- Mende in Sierra Leone
#- Esan in Nigeria

g1000 <- g1000 %>% filter(population %in% pop)

count_loci(g1000)
nrow(g1000)
```

```{r}
  sumba <- gt_load(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/GSE76645_INDONESIA_SUMBA_TIMOR.gt"))
} else {
  sumba <- gen_tibble(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/GSE76645_INDONESIA_SUMBA_TIMOR.bed"), quiet = TRUE)
}

sumba$population <- "Sumba"

timor <- read.table(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/timor"))
timor$population <- "Timor"

matching_m <- match(sumba$id, timor$V2)
sumba$population <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), timor$population[matching_m], sumba$population)

count_loci(sumba)
nrow(sumba)
```

# Create loci report

```{r}
sumba <- sumba %>% group_by(population)
loci_report_s <- qc_report_loci(sumba)
sumba <- sumba %>% ungroup()
```

```{r}
summary(loci_report_s)
autoplot(loci_report_s, type = "overview")
```

```{r}
autoplot(loci_report_s, type = "missing")
```

```{r}
sumba <- sumba %>% select_loci_if(loci_missingness(genotypes) < 0.01)
count_loci(sumba)
```

```{r}
autoplot(loci_report_s, type = "maf")
```

```{r}
sumba <- sumba %>% select_loci_if(loci_maf(genotypes) > 0.025)
count_loci(sumba)
```

```{r}
sumba <- sumba %>% select_loci_if(loci_hwe(genotypes) > 0.05)
count_loci(sumba)
```

```{r}
sumba <- sumba %>% select_loci_if(show_loci(genotypes)$chromosome %in% c(1:22))
count_loci(sumba)
```

# Create individual report

```{r}
sumba <- sumba %>% group_by(population)
individual_report_s <- qc_report_indiv(sumba, kings_threshold = 0.177)
sumba <- sumba %>% ungroup()
```

```{r}
autoplot(individual_report_s, type = "relatedness", kings_threshold = 0.177)
```

```{r}
sumba <- sumba %>% filter(id %in% individual_report_s$id & individual_report_s$to_keep == TRUE)
```

```{r}
summary(individual_report_s)
autoplot(individual_report_s)
```

This time we have individuals with higher missingness, so lets filter them out:

```{r}
sumba <- sumba %>% filter(indiv_missingness(genotypes) < 0.01)
nrow(sumba)
```

```{r}
nrow(sumba)
count_loci(sumba)
```

```{r}
}

gt_save(sumba, resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/GSE76645_INDONESIA_SUMBA_TIMOR_clean.gt"))
```
